Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Yogesh Kumar Mishra

Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the complainant.

This appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 06.02.2025 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
Saharanpur in Bail Application No. 426 of 2025, in S.S.T. No. 1258 of 2022 (State Vs. Lokesh)
arising out of Case Crime No. 02 of 2022, under Sections 384, 376, 506 I.P.C., Section 67 of I.T. Act and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Gangoh, District Saharanpur, and enlarge the appellant on bail during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: On putting query by the Court with regard to present status of trial of the appellant, it is pointed out by learned counsel for the complainant that 16.06.2025 is the date fixed for final argument before the trial court.
Learned counsel for the appellant does not dispute the said fact as pointed out by counsel for the complainant.

Looking to the stage of trial as noted above as well as dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of X vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3539, which provides that if the trial of the accused has started, his bail should not be granted in heinous offences like murder, rape and dacoity, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the appellant at this stage.

entities.text: X vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3539
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the relief as sought for by means of this criminal appeal is refused and the instant criminal appeal is dismissed.
